summary: Stephen G. Covell is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He completed his doctoral studies at Princeton University (~1995–2001) under Jacqueline I. Stone and held a post at Western Michigan University around 2003.

Sinologist Stephen H. West studied at National Taiwan Normal University and the University of Michigan (Ph.D. ~1968–1972). He served as Professor of Chinese at UC Berkeley (~1986–2004) and Arizona State University (~2004–2017), and directed the Inter-University Program.

Stephen J. Laumakis works in philosophy and Buddhist studies, having studied under John Kronen, Ramdas Lamb, George J. Tanabe, and David West. He served as an Associate Professor of Philosophy at the University of St. Thomas (attested 2008–2013).

Stephen L. Jenkins (1953–2016) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Harvard under supervisors Masatoshi Nagatomi and Charles Hallisey, and served as Professor of Religious Studies at California State Polytechnic University, Humboldt (attested 2010–2013).

Stephen Prothero is a religious studies scholar who studied at Yale (B.A. ~1978–1982) and Harvard (Ph.D. ~1986–1990 under William R. Hutchison). In ~1996, he joined Boston University, where he became Russell Professor Emeritus of Religion in America.

Stephen R. Bokenkamp, a scholar of Sinology and religious studies, studied at UC Berkeley (~1976–1986). He served at Indiana University (~1989–2007) as Associate Professor of Classical Chinese and at Arizona State University (~2007) as Professor of Chinese.
Stephen Suen is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Hong Kong under the supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2009).

Stephen Wootton Bushell (1844–1908) was a Sinologist and historian who earned his MD at the University of London (~1866–1868). He served as house surgeon at Guy's Hospital (1866) and resident medical officer at Bethlem Royal Hospital (1867).

Steve Odin is a scholar of philosophy and Japanology. After doctoral and postdoctoral work at Stony Brook University under David A. Dilworth and Edward S. Casey, he became Professor of Philosophy at the University of Hawaiʻi in 1982.

Steven Collins (1950–2018) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his D.Phil. at Oxford under Richard Gombrich. He taught at Bristol (~1980–1991) and served as Chester D. Tripp Professor at the University of Chicago from 1991.

Steven Edward Lindquist specializes in Indology and religious studies. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Texas at Austin (2005) under Patrick Olivelle, received traditional instruction from several teachers, and held a post at Concordia University.

Steven Heine is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies who studied at the University of Pennsylvania and Temple University. His posts include Pennsylvania State University (~1991–1997) and Florida International University (from 1997 as Professor).

Steven Lukes is a philosopher and sociologist who studied at Oxford under E. E. Evans-Pritchard. He held posts at Balliol College (1966–1987), European University Institute, University of Florence, University of Siena, LSE, and New York University (~2001–2021).

Steven Neal Weinberger specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his BA at Amherst and his MA and PhD (2003) at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, later holding an attested post there in 2006.

Sthaneshwar Timalsina is an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg. He held faculty posts at Nepal Sanskrit University (~1993–2003), San Diego State University (~2005–2018), and Stony Brook University (~2018).

Stig Wikander (1908–1983) was an Indologist and Iranian studies scholar who studied at Uppsala under Henrik Samuel Nyberg. He served as Docent at Lund University (1941–1953) and held the Sanskrit chair at Uppsala University (1953–1974).
Stuart H. Blackburn is an Indologist who studied at Wesleyan University and the University of California, Berkeley. He held an academic post at SOAS University of London around 1990.
Stuart McFarlane is a scholar of religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies who held an appointment in the Department of Religious Studies at Lancaster University (attested 1991 and 2001).

Stuart Piggott (1910–1996) was an archaeologist and Indologist. He studied under Mortimer Wheeler at University College London and the UCL Institute of Archaeology (~1934–1936), later holding a post at the University of Edinburgh (~1946–1977).

Stuart Ray Sarbacker works in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 2001 under David M. Knipe and held a post at Oregon State University (attested 2018).
